headline: Sound Like a Native · Core 30
threshold: Carry clear consonant–vowel patterns into natural Spanish words, phrases, and conversation.

lessons.title: B and v together
lessons.objective: Recognize that b/v spelling does not normally mark different Spanish phonemes.
lessons.focus: Compare ba bi bu be bo after a pause with the b/v family between vowels. Do not use English upper-teeth/lower-lip v as the default Spanish target.

words.es: Beatriz busca una bolsa verde para la fruta.
words.en: Beatriz looks for a green bag for the fruit.

words.es: El vendedor ofrece una bolsa blanca más grande.
words.en: The seller offers a larger white bag.

words.es: Beatriz compra una uva para probarla.
words.en: Beatriz buys a grape to taste it.

words.es: También pide una bebida para el viaje.
words.en: She also asks for a drink for the trip.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, recognize that b/v spelling does not normally mark different Spanish phonemes. Use the scene: A bag of fruit. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Dental t and d
lessons.objective: Place both sounds near the upper teeth and compare voicing.
lessons.focus: Compare ta ti tu te to with da di du de do. Keep a light dental contact and notice the voicing difference instead of pressing harder.

words.es: Diana prepara dos tazas de té.
words.en: Diana prepares two cups of tea.

words.es: Toca una taza con el dedo para comprobar la temperatura.
words.en: She touches a cup with her finger to check the temperature.

words.es: Todavía está caliente y la deja en la mesa.
words.en: It is still hot and she leaves it on the table.

words.es: Su tía llega durante el día.
words.en: Her aunt arrives during the day.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, place both sounds near the upper teeth and compare voicing. Use the scene: Two cups for the visit. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: D in connected speech
lessons.objective: Hear and practise contextual d realizations with a speaker model.
lessons.focus: Compare d after a pause and d inside cada día. Follow a model for the lighter intervocalic gesture; do not turn a context effect into a rule to delete every d.

words.es: Cada día Daniel pasa por la panadería.
words.en: Every day Daniel stops by the bakery.

words.es: Da su pedido a la señora del mostrador.
words.en: He gives his order to the woman at the counter.

words.es: La señora deja el pan al lado de la caja.
words.en: The woman leaves the bread beside the register.

words.es: Daniel busca una moneda en el bolsillo.
words.en: Daniel looks for a coin in his pocket.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, hear and practise contextual d realizations with a speaker model. Use the scene: Every day at the bakery. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: G in connected speech
lessons.objective: Compare a firm onset with a more open g between vowels.
lessons.focus: Compare ga after a pause with g inside lago and amigo. Notice the more open contextual gesture without treating every written g as the same closure.

words.es: Mi amigo guarda agua en la mochila.
words.en: My friend puts water in the backpack.

words.es: Seguimos el camino que llega al lago.
words.en: We follow the path that reaches the lake.

words.es: Un gato gris camina cerca del agua.
words.en: A gray cat walks near the water.

words.es: Mi amigo saca un abrigo porque hace frío.
words.en: My friend takes out a coat because it is cold.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, compare a firm onset with a more open g between vowels. Use the scene: The lake and the cat. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: The single r tap
lessons.objective: Make a brief tongue contact in the right word context.
lessons.focus: Use a quick single tongue-tip contact in ara iri uru ere oro. Keep the tap between vowels; initial written r belongs to the trill family.

words.es: Miro una pera en el mercado.
words.en: I look at a pear at the market.

words.es: El vendedor me dice que hoy está cara.
words.en: The seller tells me that it is expensive today.

words.es: Busco dinero y comparo el precio de otra pera.
words.en: I look for money and compare the price of another pear.

words.es: Un amigo mira mi cara y se ríe.
words.en: A friend looks at my face and laughs.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, make a brief tongue contact in the right word context. Use the scene: An expensive pear. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: The trill and initial r
lessons.objective: Build a trill gradually and recognize word-initial r.
lessons.focus: Use ra ri ru re ro for initial r and compare carro with a model. Keep the tongue tip relaxed; return to a slower pattern if the trill becomes forced.

words.es: El carro rojo está junto al río.
words.en: The red car is beside the river.

words.es: Rosa mira una rama que bloquea la ruta.
words.en: Rosa looks at a branch that blocks the route.

words.es: Su hermano retira la rama con cuidado.
words.en: Her brother removes the branch carefully.

words.es: Luego Rosa revisa el carro antes de regresar.
words.en: Then Rosa checks the car before returning.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, build a trill gradually and recognize word-initial r. Use the scene: A red car by the river. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: R contrasts that change meaning
lessons.objective: Identify and produce tap/trill contrasts in context.
lessons.focus: Alternate the single tap in caro with the trill in carro, then pero/perro. Prioritize the meaning contrast before any timed run.

words.es: Pregunto por el carro que está cerca de la puerta.
words.en: I ask about the car near the door.

words.es: El empleado entiende caro y me habla del precio.
words.en: The employee hears expensive and tells me about the price.

words.es: Repito carro con calma para aclarar la pregunta.
words.en: I repeat car calmly to clarify the question.

words.es: Hay un perro al lado del mostrador.
words.en: There is a dog beside the counter.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, identify and produce tap/trill contrasts in context. Use the scene: A clarification at the desk. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: S, c, and z in the chosen model
lessons.objective: Use seseo while preserving standard spelling.
lessons.focus: Use sa si su se so for the chosen seseo model. Casa/caza sound alike in this model but remain different words and spellings.

words.es: Busco una casa cerca del centro.
words.en: I look for a house near the center.

words.es: La dueña prepara la cena cuando llego.
words.en: The owner is making dinner when I arrive.

words.es: Dejo un zapato mojado junto a la entrada.
words.en: I leave a wet shoe beside the entrance.

words.es: En la pared hay un dibujo de una escena de caza.
words.en: On the wall there is a drawing of a hunting scene.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use seseo while preserving standard spelling. Use the scene: A house and a small garden. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: J and g before e/i
lessons.objective: Recognize one sound family with different spellings and regional realizations.
lessons.focus: Practise ja ji ju je jo with the chosen regional model. Map ge/gi words to this family and accept a lighter regional realization rather than forcing harsh friction.

words.es: La gente espera en el jardín del café.
words.en: People wait in the café garden.

words.es: Un joven pide una jarra de agua.
words.en: A young person asks for a pitcher of water.

words.es: La encargada ofrece jugo de naranja también.
words.en: The person in charge also offers orange juice.

words.es: El joven elige jugo y se sienta junto a la ventana.
words.en: The young person chooses juice and sits beside the window.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, recognize one sound family with different spellings and regional realizations. Use the scene: A jug of juice. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Y and ll
lessons.objective: Use a consistent model and recognize regional alternatives.
lessons.focus: Use ya yi yu ye yo as a pattern cue, then a consistent yeísta word model. Regional y/ll realizations belong in listening comparisons, not in an error list.

words.es: Yo busco la llave antes de salir.
words.en: I look for the key before leaving.

words.es: La lluvia cae sobre la calle vacía.
words.en: Rain falls on the empty street.

words.es: Llevo una bolsa con yuca para la cena.
words.en: I carry a bag of cassava for dinner.

words.es: Mi hermana llama desde la puerta.
words.en: My sister calls from the doorway.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use a consistent model and recognize regional alternatives. Use the scene: A key for the rainy evening. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Written h and spoken vowels
lessons.objective: Read common silent h words without inserting a consonant.
lessons.focus: Use whole words with ordinary silent h rather than adding a breath consonant. Keep the vowel attached to a neighboring consonant during the warm-up patter.

words.es: Digo hola al entrar en el hotel.
words.en: I say hello as I enter the hotel.

words.es: Pregunto a qué hora llega mi hermano.
words.en: I ask what time my brother arrives.

words.es: La recepcionista mira la hora en la pantalla.
words.en: The receptionist looks at the time on the screen.

words.es: Me dice que puedo esperar aquí ahora.
words.en: She tells me that I can wait here now.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, read common silent h words without inserting a consonant. Use the scene: A greeting at the hotel. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: When the u is heard
lessons.objective: Contrast gu with gü before e/i.
lessons.focus: Contrast silent u in gue/gui with audible u in güe/güi. Move through gue gui güe güi inside model words; the written marks matter.

words.es: La guía trae una foto de un pingüino.
words.en: The guide brings a photograph of a penguin.

words.es: Un niño señala una guitarra en otra página.
words.en: A child points to a guitar on another page.

words.es: La guía explica la palabra guerra con cuidado.
words.en: The guide explains the word war carefully.

words.es: Al niño le da vergüenza leer delante del grupo.
words.en: The child feels embarrassed about reading in front of the group.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, contrast gu with gü before e/i. Use the scene: A guide with a penguin picture. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: X and place names
lessons.objective: Learn context and name-specific pronunciations without inventing a universal rule.
lessons.focus: Compare x in taxi/examen with the name México. Practise the actual words; do not infer one sound for every x or every place name.

words.es: Tengo un examen de lectura en México.
words.en: I have a reading exam in Mexico.

words.es: Tomo un taxi para llegar a tiempo.
words.en: I take a taxi to arrive on time.

words.es: Durante el viaje reviso un texto corto.
words.en: During the trip I review a short text.

words.es: El conductor me desea éxito en el examen.
words.en: The driver wishes me success in the exam.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, learn context and name-specific pronunciations without inventing a universal rule. Use the scene: A taxi in Mexico. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Closed syllables
lessons.objective: Finish common word-final consonants without adding a vowel.
lessons.focus: Move from CV patter into pan, sol, sal, papel, mes without adding a final vowel. Keep the closure or narrowing appropriate to the word ending.

words.es: Este mes hacemos un picnic cerca del río.
words.en: This month we have a picnic near the river.

words.es: Llevo pan y un poco de sal.
words.en: I bring bread and a little salt.

words.es: Mi amigo envuelve la comida en papel.
words.en: My friend wraps the food in paper.

words.es: Buscamos sombra porque hace mucho sol.
words.en: We look for shade because it is very sunny.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, finish common word-final consonants without adding a vowel. Use the scene: Bread for the picnic. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Initial es clusters
lessons.objective: Read the written initial vowel and avoid deleting it.
lessons.focus: Keep the written initial e in escuela/español. Link the existing e to the s cluster without adding a second vowel inside the cluster.

words.es: La estación está cerca de la escuela.
words.en: The station is near the school.

words.es: Una estudiante pregunta por la clase de español.
words.en: A student asks about the Spanish class.

words.es: Le digo que siga hasta la esquina.
words.en: I tell her to continue to the corner.

words.es: Después debe subir por la escalera de la entrada.
words.en: Then she must go up the entrance stairs.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, read the written initial vowel and avoid deleting it. Use the scene: The station by the school. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: N changes its place
lessons.objective: Notice nasal place changes in connected speech without changing spelling.
lessons.focus: Compare un beso, un gato, un día with a model. Notice that the nasal contact adapts to the next consonant while the written n remains.

words.es: Antes de salir, Ana le da un beso a su mamá.
words.en: Before leaving, Ana gives her mom a kiss.

words.es: Lleva una carta con su nombre al banco.
words.en: She takes a letter with her name to the bank.

words.es: Un gato duerme al lado de la puerta.
words.en: A cat sleeps beside the door.

words.es: Su mamá pregunta qué día vuelve su hermano.
words.en: Her mom asks what day her brother returns.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, notice nasal place changes in connected speech without changing spelling. Use the scene: A message before leaving. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Pr and br clusters
lessons.objective: Keep the cluster together without adding an extra vowel.
lessons.focus: Move through pra pri pru pre pro and bra bri bru bre bro without inserting a vowel inside the consonant cluster. Release into one clear following vowel.

words.es: Mi primo llega pronto a la librería.
words.en: My cousin arrives at the bookstore soon.

words.es: Lleva un libro debajo del brazo.
words.en: He carries a book under his arm.

words.es: Preguntamos el precio de otro libro para la clase.
words.en: We ask the price of another book for the class.

words.es: La empleada nos muestra una edición más pequeña.
words.en: The employee shows us a smaller edition.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, keep the cluster together without adding an extra vowel. Use the scene: A cousin with a white bag. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Tr and dr clusters
lessons.objective: Move from dental closure into the r gesture.
lessons.focus: Practise tra tri tru tre tro and dra dri dru dre dro with light contact. Follow the chosen speaker model; do not force an extra vowel between consonants.

words.es: Tres personas esperan en la entrada de la estación.
words.en: Three people wait at the station entrance.

words.es: Mi madre pregunta a qué hora sale el tren.
words.en: My mother asks what time the train leaves.

words.es: Un trabajador nos indica el andén correcto.
words.en: A worker points us to the right platform.

words.es: Hay una piedra pequeña junto a la escalera.
words.en: There is a small stone beside the stairs.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, move from dental closure into the r gesture. Use the scene: Three people at the station. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Cr and gr clusters
lessons.objective: Build a velar-to-r cluster in a real word.
lessons.focus: Practise cra cri cru cre cro and gra gri gru gre gro. Keep the cluster compact, then say a complete phrase with ordinary stress.

words.es: Un grupo grande llega a la plaza.
words.en: A large group arrives at the square.

words.es: La guía señala una cruz sobre la puerta de la iglesia.
words.en: The guide points to a cross above the church door.

words.es: Después el grupo entra en un café pequeño.
words.en: Then the group goes into a small café.

words.es: Una persona pide crema para su café.
words.en: One person asks for cream for their coffee.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, build a velar-to-r cluster in a real word. Use the scene: A large group at the crossing. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Clusters with l
lessons.objective: Keep pl/bl/fl/cl/gl as clusters.
lessons.focus: Practise pla pli plu ple plo, then switch to bla/fla/cla/gla with the same vowel order. Keep the l joined to the preceding consonant.

words.es: Clara prepara un plato blanco para la fiesta.
words.en: Clara sets out a white plate for the party.

words.es: Pone una flor cerca de cada plato.
words.en: She puts a flower near each plate.

words.es: Un globo azul cuelga junto a la ventana.
words.en: A blue balloon hangs beside the window.

words.es: Sus amigos llegan después de la clase.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, keep pl/bl/fl/cl/gl as clusters. Use the scene: A white plate and a flower. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Finding syllables
lessons.objective: Use helpful syllable divisions without treating every letter as one beat.
lessons.focus: Use whole-word chunks: ca-sa, es-cue-la, trans-por-te. Keep the existing consonants and vowels; spelling letters do not each receive a separate beat.

words.es: Miro el mapa del transporte de la ciudad.
words.en: I look at the city transport map.

words.es: La escuela está al final de un camino corto.
words.en: The school is at the end of a short route.

words.es: Divido las palabras del mapa en partes fáciles de decir.
words.en: I divide the map words into easy-to-say parts.

words.es: Después digo transporte sin añadir una vocal al final.
words.en: Then I say transport without adding a vowel at the end.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use helpful syllable divisions without treating every letter as one beat. Use the scene: A route through the city. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Default word stress
lessons.objective: Use ordinary stress patterns as a reading aid.
lessons.focus: Contrast the stress in ME-sa and pa-PEL inside whole words. Use regular stress patterns as reading clues, then check exceptions and actual speech.

words.es: El joven deja un papel sobre la mesa.
words.en: The young person leaves a piece of paper on the table.

words.es: El papel tiene un mensaje para Marta.
words.en: The paper has a message for Marta.

words.es: Marta mira el reloj y busca a su hermano.
words.en: Marta looks at her watch and looks for her brother.

words.es: Su hermano escucha el mensaje sin interrumpir.
words.en: Her brother listens to the message without interrupting.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use ordinary stress patterns as a reading aid. Use the scene: A message on the table. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Written accents
lessons.objective: Use an accent mark to locate stress and notice exceptions.
lessons.focus: Let the written accent identify the stressed syllable in café, médico, fácil, número, teléfono. Keep clear vowels in the unstressed syllables too.

words.es: El médico me llama por mi nombre.
words.en: The doctor calls me by my name.

words.es: Confirmo mi número de teléfono en la recepción.
words.en: I confirm my telephone number at reception.

words.es: La recepcionista dice que el formulario es fácil.
words.en: The receptionist says that the form is easy.

words.es: Después de la cita tomo un café cerca de la clínica.
words.en: After the appointment I have a coffee near the clinic.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, use an accent mark to locate stress and notice exceptions. Use the scene: Coffee after the appointment. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Moving stress, changing meaning
lessons.objective: Hear stress as a word-level contrast.
lessons.focus: Contrast público, publico, publicó as whole words. Move stress without deliberately changing the vowel inventory; explain the meaning each form carries.

words.es: El público espera una noticia antes del concierto.
words.en: The audience waits for some news before the concert.

words.es: La directora publicó un aviso esta mañana.
words.en: The director published a notice this morning.

words.es: Yo publico los horarios en la página del teatro.
words.en: I publish the schedules on the theater website.

words.es: El aviso explica que la puerta abre más tarde.
words.en: The notice explains that the door opens later.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, hear stress as a word-level contrast. Use the scene: An announcement for the audience. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Vowels in one syllable
lessons.objective: Practise common diphthongs from real speaker models.
lessons.focus: Practise vowel combinations inside tierra, puerta, aire, agua, tiempo. Use speaker models for the glide; keep the warm-up consonant-linked rather than isolating vowels.

words.es: La puerta del jardín está abierta.
Hay agua sobre la tierra cerca de la entrada.
words.en: There is water on the ground near the entrance.

words.es: El aire está fresco después de la lluvia.
words.en: The air is cool after the rain.

words.es: Tengo tiempo para caminar antes de comer.
words.en: I have time to walk before eating.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, practise common diphthongs from real speaker models. Use the scene: A door beside the water. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Vowels across syllables
lessons.objective: Keep the contrast between common hiatus and diphthong examples.
lessons.focus: Use país, día, poeta and alegría to practise vowel sequences in their words. Notice syllable boundaries and stress without adding a consonant or forcing equal beats.

words.es: Cada día leo un poema antes de salir.
words.en: Every day I read a poem before leaving.

words.es: Hoy el poeta describe un viaje a otro país.
words.en: Today the poet describes a trip to another country.

words.es: Su poema habla de la alegría de volver a casa.
words.en: The poem speaks of the joy of returning home.

words.es: Leo despacio las palabras país y día.
words.en: I read the words country and day slowly.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, keep the contrast between common hiatus and diphthong examples. Use the scene: A poem for the day. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Vowel-to-vowel linking
lessons.objective: Join words smoothly while keeping the message clear.
lessons.focus: Warm up with ma mi mu me mo, then join mi amigo, la otra, tengo una idea. Let the words connect while keeping the intended vowels and meaning clear.

words.es: Mi amigo llega una hora antes de la salida.
words.en: My friend arrives an hour before departure.

words.es: Tengo una idea para aprovechar el tiempo.
words.en: I have an idea for making use of the time.

words.es: Podemos esperar en la otra entrada del parque.
words.en: We can wait at the other park entrance.

words.es: Mi amigo acepta y compra una botella de agua.
words.en: My friend agrees and buys a bottle of water.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, join words smoothly while keeping the message clear. Use the scene: An idea for a shared outing. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Consonant-to-vowel linking
lessons.objective: Let a final consonant flow into the next vowel.
lessons.focus: Move from na ni nu ne no into un amigo and los amigos. Let final consonants flow into the following vowel without changing the written words.

words.es: Los amigos esperan en la entrada del restaurante.
words.en: The friends wait at the restaurant entrance.

words.es: Un amigo pregunta cuánto dura la espera.
words.en: A friend asks how long the wait is.

words.es: La encargada busca una mesa para el grupo.
words.en: The person in charge looks for a table for the group.

words.es: Dice que hay sitio cerca de una ventana.
words.en: She says that there is room near a window.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, let a final consonant flow into the next vowel. Use the scene: Friends at the entrance. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Meaning groups
lessons.objective: Pause at phrase boundaries rather than between every word.
lessons.focus: Say a familiar CV row, then group words by meaning. Pause after a useful phrase, not after every word; avoid imposing drill beats on ordinary speech.

words.es: Mañana por la mañana vamos al mercado.
words.en: Tomorrow morning we are going to the market.

words.es: Antes de salir, envío un mensaje al grupo.
words.en: Before leaving, I send a message to the group.

words.es: Explico el lugar de encuentro y hago una pausa.
words.en: I explain the meeting place and pause.

words.es: Después digo a qué hora debemos regresar.
words.en: Then I say what time we must return.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, pause at phrase boundaries rather than between every word. Use the scene: Tomorrow morning's plan. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

lessons.title: Core transfer check
lessons.objective: Read and speak a new scene with sound, stress, and linking targets.
lessons.focus: Use a mixed warm-up, then read the new message once and retell it. Self-check one sound target, word stress, and meaningful pauses separately.

words.es: Hay un cambio de lugar para la reunión.
words.en: There is a change of location for the meeting.

words.es: Leo el mensaje y miro el camino en el mapa.
words.en: I read the message and look at the route on the map.

words.es: La hora sigue igual pero la entrada es diferente.
words.en: The time stays the same but the entrance is different.

words.es: Llamo a una persona del grupo para explicar el cambio.
words.en: I call someone in the group to explain the change.

lessons.speaking: In Spanish, read and speak a new scene with sound, stress, and linking targets. Use the scene: A changed meeting place. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.
